## Resolver polish: LSP readiness-wait so heavy servers… — 2026-07-29 (parent 34bb7862ad85)

A new `Resolver` dataclass (`enabled`, `disabled_languages`, `servers`) is added to `trie/config.py` and wired into `Config.from_dict` and `DEFAULT_CONFIG_TOML`. `Scope.include` is extended to cover JS/JSX/MJS/CJS, Go, Rust, C/H, and Lua files by default.

`LspServerSpec` gains `init_timeout`, `warmup`, and `ready_timeout` fields; `LspResolver` adds `_await_ready` polling so heavy servers (rust-analyzer, gopls, clangd) are not queried before their workspace index is ready, and warm clients are reused via a per-source-root cache.

`specs.py` adds `configure_resolver`/`_apply_config` plus module-level `_ENABLED`, `_DISABLED_LANGUAGES`, `_SERVER_OVERRIDES` state; `C_SPEC`, `GO_SPEC`, `LUA_SPEC`, `RUST_SPEC` gain readiness timeouts. `registry.apply_resolver_config` pushes config into specs and resets backend caches; `scan_project` calls it before parsing.

New additions:
- `scripts/bench_resolver.py` — language-agnostic benchmark comparing tree-sitter-only vs tree-sitter+LSP edge counts and method-edge recall
- `test_resolver_defaults`, `test_resolver_overrides`, `test_resolver_config_gates_specs` in `tests/test_config.py`

- + scripts/bench_resolver:_project_qnames — "Collect all qualified symbol names from `files` by extracting symbols via the registry, silently skipping files that raise exceptions."
